options: The result is shown on the monitor
The CPU gets the next instruction from memory
The CPU works out what the instruction means
The CPU carries out the instruction

questions.q: What is the purpose of cache memory?
options: To connect the computer to the internet
To hold frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU for fast access

questions.q: Data in ROM is lost when the power is switched off.
questions.explain: ROM is non-volatile: it keeps its data without power.

questions.q: An SSD has no moving parts.
Utility software is a type of application software used to write letters.
questions.explain: Utility software is system software that maintains or protects the computer (e.g. antivirus, backup, compression).

questions.q: The ALU carries out calculations and logical comparisons.
The ____ stores programs and data that are currently in use and is cleared when the power is off.
A hard disk drive stores data on spinning ____ disks.
Software that manages the computer's hardware and other software is called the ____.
CPU clock speed is measured in hertz; modern CPUs run at billions of hertz, or ____ (GHz).
Describe the three stages of the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
questions.answer: Fetch: the CPU gets an instruction from memory (1). Decode: the control unit works out what the instruction means (1). Execute: the instruction is carried out (1).

questions.q: State two differences between RAM and ROM.
questions.answer: Any two from: RAM is volatile (loses data when power is off) but ROM is non-volatile; RAM can be read and written but ROM is normally read-only; RAM holds programs and data in use but ROM holds start-up instructions (boot).

questions.q: Give two examples of embedded systems and say what each one controls.
questions.answer: Any two, each with a function, e.g. washing machine (controls the wash cycle); microwave oven (controls time and power); traffic lights (controls the light sequence); digital watch (keeps time).

pairs: Manages the hardware and runs programs
